questions.prompt: A 5 kg box on a floor with mu_s = 0.6 is pushed horizontally with 25 N and does not move. What is the friction force?

remediationRefs.label: Review: Static friction is a reaction

questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to balance the applied force up to mu_s*N; here 25 N < 29.43 N.

questions.prompt: A block sits on a 20 degree slope with mu_s = 0.5, mu_k = 0.4. It has mass 2 kg. What is the friction force in N (three decimals, g = 9.81)?
questions.explanation: tan 20 = 0.364 < 0.5 so it sticks and friction equals the down-slope pull m g sin(theta) = 6.710 N.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg block sits on a 30 degree slope with mu_s = 0.5, mu_k = 0.4 (g = 9.81). What is the down-slope acceleration in m/s^2 (three decimals)?
questions.explanation: tan 30 = 0.577 > 0.5: sliding, a = g(sin - mu_k cos) = 1.507.

questions.prompt: Which condition describes the normal force of rigid unilateral contact?
options: Gap >= 0, force >= 0 and gap times force = 0
Force can be negative if the gap is positive

questions.prompt: A 2 kg mass rests on a floor (gap 0, velocity 0). With time step h = 0.01 s the complementarity contact force is computed. What is it in N (two decimals, g = 9.81)?
questions.explanation: phi_free = -g h^2, lambda = -phi_free m / h^2 = m g = 19.62 N.

questions.prompt: A tall narrow box is pushed near its top on a high-friction floor. It tips before it slides when:
questions.explanation: Slide force mu_s m g exceeds the tip force m g w/(2H) when mu_s > w/(2H).

questions.prompt: A simulated block slides with mu_k = 0.3 and never comes to rest; its velocity oscillates about zero. Explain the cause and give two fixes.
rubric: Identifies explicit sign(v) friction overshooting zero (chatter of order mu g h).
Names a fix such as clamping friction to stop at v = 0, or solving stick as a complementarity condition.
Names another fix such as regularising the sign function and notes its small creep error.
